title: Modi to Unveil Rs 34,470 Crore of Bihar Projects on Three-State Saturday Tour
excerpt: The Prime Minister's Saturday runs from IIT Kharagpur's 75th anniversary to a Rs 34,470 crore Bihar programme centred on the Nitish Setu Ganga bridge, and ends at the national skills ceremony in Lucknow.
body:
• Prime Minister Narendra Modi visits three states on Saturday: IIT Kharagpur's Platinum Jubilee in West Bengal, project launches in Bihar's Vaishali, and the Kaushal Deekshant Samaroh in Lucknow, according to an official press release reported by IANS.
  • The Bihar programme is the day's centrepiece: projects worth around Rs 34,470 crore to be inaugurated, dedicated or founded, including the Rs 4,280 crore Nitish Setu bridge over the Ganga.
  • More than Rs 15,600 crore of projects will be inaugurated — among them a 660 MW unit of the Buxar Thermal Power Project — and foundation stones laid for around Rs 14,450 crore more.
  • For readers with family in Bihar: the day also brings 100 PM-eBus electric buses and Griha Pravesh ceremonies for more than 26,900 PMAY-Urban beneficiaries.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi will spend Saturday moving across three states — West Bengal, Bihar and Uttar Pradesh — in a day built around an institutional anniversary, a large Bihar infrastructure programme and a national skills ceremony, according to an official press release reported by IANS via The Freedom Press and the Prime Minister's official site.

The itinerary

The day begins in West Bengal. The Prime Minister will reach IIT Kharagpur at around 9:45 a.m. to participate in the institute's Platinum Jubilee celebrations, address the gathering and interact with 75 students, symbolising the institution's 75-year journey. Established in 1951, IIT Kharagpur was the first Indian Institute of Technology set up in the country and is recognised as an Institute of National Importance.

He then travels to Bihar, visiting Nitish Setu in Vaishali district at around 1:15 p.m. At around 2 p.m. he will inaugurate and dedicate development projects to the nation and lay the foundation stone of several others, with a combined value of approximately Rs 34,470 crore, and address the gathering. The final stop is Uttar Pradesh: at around 5:30 p.m. he will participate in the 5th Kaushal Deekshant Samaroh at Indira Gandhi Pratishthan in Gomti Nagar, Lucknow.

What the Rs 34,470 crore in Bihar covers

The projects span road connectivity, energy, urban infrastructure, water resources, education, healthcare and transport, according to Indian Witness. The headline item is Nitish Setu, an extradosed cable-stayed bridge across the Ganga built at an estimated cost of Rs 4,280 crore. The 19.7 km project connects Kachhi Dargah on National Highway 22 in Patna district with Bidupur on National Highway 322 in Vaishali district, and the Prime Minister's office says it will reduce travel time between North and South Bihar.

Projects worth more than Rs 15,600 crore will be inaugurated. They include the six-laning of the Aurangabad-Chordaha stretch of NH-19, the Chorma-Bairgania section of NH-227F and the Umagaon-Saharsa section of NH-327, the commissioning of Unit 2 of the Buxar Thermal Power Project with a capacity of 660 MW, electricity distribution works, canal restoration, a floating solar project at Phulwaria Dam and sewerage facilities. Foundation stones will be laid for projects worth approximately Rs 14,450 crore across road, power, water-supply and educational infrastructure.

Two parts of the Bihar programme reach households directly. The Prime Minister will flag off 100 electric buses under the PM-eBus initiative, and a Griha Pravesh ceremony will be held for more than 26,900 beneficiaries under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana-Urban.

The Lucknow close

The Kaushal Deekshant Samaroh, instituted in the academic session 2021-22, is an annual national platform to recognise excellence in skill development. This year, 52 national-level toppers from Industrial Training Institutes, National Skill Training Institutes and Institutes for Training of Trainers will be felicitated, according to the official release.

All three programmes are scheduled for Saturday, November 21; the Bihar project figures are the government's announced values for projects being inaugurated or founded on the day, not completed-project outturn costs.
